findings.message: adding column users.created fails on SQLite: non-constant DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
findings.guidance:
SQLite's ADD COLUMN cannot: declare PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE; use a
non-constant default (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, expressions in parentheses); be NOT
NULL without a non-NULL default; be a STORED generated column; or REFERENCE
another table while having a non-NULL default when foreign keys are on.

Either relax the definition (add the column nullable, backfill, then treat
NOT NULL in the application) or rebuild the table with the column in its
CREATE TABLE (see sqlite-unsupported-alter for the procedure).
findings.statement: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

findings.message: ALTER TABLE form SQLite does not support: near "TYPE": syntax error
findings.statement: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN name TYPE VARCHAR(10)

findings.guidance:
Running application code (and ORM/sqlc-generated code with cached column lists)
still references the column and fails once it is gone.

Safe sequence:
  1. Remove every read and write of the column from the application and deploy.
  2. Then, in a later migration, drop the column:

     ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN name;

If the column is already unused, add "-- safe_sql:disable ban-drop-column"
above the statement to acknowledge this.
findings.statement: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN code

findings.message: DROP COLUMN users.code fails on SQLite: it is a key or indexed
findings.guidance:
SQLite added DROP COLUMN in 3.35.0, and even then refuses to drop a column
that is a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE, has an index, is referenced by a foreign key
or a generated column, or appears in a view or trigger. The statement fails
at run time with the migration half applied.

Drop the dependent index, view or trigger first (and recreate it), or rebuild
the table without the column (see sqlite-unsupported-alter).
findings.statement: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN code

findings.message: PRAGMA foreign_keys inside a transaction has no effect
rebuilding users copies every row under the write lock
findings.guidance:
SQLite has one writer at a time. Copying a large table into its
replacement holds the write lock (and, without WAL, blocks readers) until
the transaction commits. Schedule the migration for a quiet period, and
prefer WAL mode so readers keep working.

findings.message: rebuild of users does not recreate: view user_names
rebuild does not run PRAGMA foreign_key_check before COMMIT
